name: John

notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Irving; https://globalnews.ca/news/62776/n-b-business-magnate-jack-irving-dead-at-78/). Input name is only 'John'; identified via shared_with Irving brothers. Business interests passed to son John K.F. Irving.

notes: Deceased (source: https://www.myjewishlearning.com/2013/12/22/mourning-edgar-m-bronfman/). Forbes 2001-2009 entry assumed to be Edgar Sr. (son Edgar Jr. was not separately a Forbes billionaire then).

name: Ted Arison
profile: Founder of Carnival Cruise Lines (1972) and co-founder of Norwegian Caribbean Lines. Died October 1, 1999 in Tel Aviv, aged 75.

name: Stephen D. Jr. And Riley P. Bechtel
current_role: Riley P. Bechtel: non-executive director (former chairman & CEO), Bechtel Corporation. Stephen D. Bechtel Jr.: deceased.
profile: Joint Forbes entry for father and son owners of Bechtel, the San Francisco engineering and construction giant. Stephen Jr. ran the firm 1960-1990 and died March 15, 2021 aged 95. Riley, his son and great-grandson of founder Warren Bechtel, was CEO 1990-2014 and chairman to 2017, then stayed on as a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: Riley Bechtel first worked summers at the company starting in 1966, joined full-time in 1981 and was CEO by 1990, making him the fourth generation of the family to lead it.
notes: Mixed entry: Stephen D. Bechtel Jr. died 2021 (https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/retired-chairman-and-ceo-stephen-d-bechtel-jr-dies-at-95-301247806.html). Riley P. Bechtel alive per available sources; he stepped back as CEO in 2014 for health reasons. Very private family; Bechtel corporate media team is the only route.

name: Jacques
current_role: Former chairman / supervisory board president, Louis Delhaize Group (Belgium; now renamed LDz)
profile: Jacques Bouriez (identified via shared_with Philippe Bouriez and source Louis Delhaize) is a member of the Bouriez family that controls Belgian retailer Louis Delhaize, owner of the Cora and Match hypermarkets. He chaired/oversaw the group's supervisory board after his brother Philippe stepped back in 2009. The group sold Cora/Match France to Carrefour (2023-24) and Delitraiteur to Colruyt (2024).
interesting_fact: The family group, founded in 1875 in Charleroi, sold its French Cora and Match chains to Carrefour, closing in July 2024.
notes: Input gives only first name 'Jacques'; identity inferred as Jacques Bouriez. No recent public info; current status and age (likely 80s) unconfirmed. Next generation (Pierre and François Bouriez) runs the business. Very low public profile.

name: Hermann Langness
current_role: Owner, Bartels-Langness (Bela) retail group, Kiel; withdrawing from day-to-day management (2026)
profile: Hermann Langness is the owner of Bartels-Langness (Bela), a fifth-generation family food retailer and wholesaler headquartered in Kiel that runs famila hypermarkets and supplies Markant/nah & frisch stores in northern and eastern Germany. In January 2026 the group announced a new structure as he steps further back and eldest son Fritz Langness (at Bela since 2014) takes on more responsibility.
interesting_fact: Bela has been run by the same family from Kiel for five generations and operates around 82 famila large-format stores.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Only on Forbes list 2017-2018. Best route is Bela press office; succession now with son Fritz Langness.

name: Danny Harris
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner, Alo Yoga / Color Image Apparel (Los Angeles)
profile: Danny Harris co-owns athleisure brand Alo Yoga with childhood friend Marco DeGeorge. The pair grew up in Los Gatos, CA, launched screen-printing wholesaler Color Image Apparel in 1992 (parent of blank-tee maker Bella+Canvas) and created Alo in 2007. Alo drove most of the group's ~$2B 2024 revenue and has 150+ stores worldwide.
interesting_fact: The name Alo stands for 'air, land, ocean'; the brand grew out of DeGeorge turning to yoga to recover from childhood back surgery, with Harris joining him.
deep_cut_fact: Before graduating high school, Harris and DeGeorge were already screen-printing shirts for a local business in Los Gatos, the side hustle that became Color Image Apparel.
notes: Very low personal media profile; Alo has an in-house PR team but no published press email (only customer-service addresses). Best route is via Alo corporate PR.

name: Luo Yuhao
current_role: Co-founder and vice president, miHoYo (HoYoverse), Shanghai
profile: Luo Yuhao (罗宇皓) co-founded Shanghai game studio miHoYo in 2012 with Shanghai Jiao Tong University classmates Cai Haoyu and Liu Wei. Early on he handled monetization and game-economy/progression design. miHoYo's anime-style hits Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero made all three founders billionaires; Luo remains VP and keeps an extremely low profile.
interesting_fact: In 2026 the three miHoYo founders jointly funded an 'AI Future Cornerstone' fund at their alma mater Shanghai Jiao Tong University's School of Artificial Intelligence.
deep_cut_fact: The 'HoYo' in miHoYo comes from the H and Y initials shared by founders Cai Haoyu and Luo Yuhao's given names (浩宇/宇皓); 'mi' was added from Hatsune Miku when HoYo turned out to be taken.

public_contacts.value: rui.lu@mihoyo.com (miHoYo media contact listed on 2021 press release; may be outdated)

notes: Almost never gives interviews or appears publicly; Liu Wei is the founders' public face. Deep-cut source is a fan wiki (Moegirlpedia) - verify before use. Press email is a named PR staffer from a 2021 release.

name: Sergei Galitsky
current_role: Owner and president, FC Krasnodar (football club and academy); founder of Magnit
profile: Sergey Galitsky founded Magnit, one of Russia's largest grocery and cosmetics chains, after starting as a perfume/cosmetics wholesaler (Tander) in 1994; he opened the first store in 1998 and took it public in 2006. He sold almost all his stake to VTB in 2018 for $2.4B and now focuses on FC Krasnodar, its academy, a stadium, a 2,500-tree park and a family winery.
interesting_fact: An admirer of Walmart, he advertised his first Magnit store with the slogan 'Always Low Prices'; he later spent ~$460M on FC Krasnodar's stadium (nicknamed the 'Galiseum') and $70M on the adjacent park.
deep_cut_fact: A teenage chess talent, he became a candidate master within two years and won the Sochi championship; he made chess compulsory at the FC Krasnodar academy and in 2013 played a 4-hour simul vs 20 pupils, winning 16.5-3.5.

public_contacts.value: n.baiburin@fckrasnodar.ru (head of FC Krasnodar press service)

notes: Russia-based; check current sanctions/compliance status before outreach. Known as outspoken and relatively accessible to press in Russian media (e.g. Novaya Gazeta 2025 interview). Born Sergey Arutyunyan, 1967.

name: Johnny Boufarhat
current_role: Founder, Hopin (stepped down as CEO 2023); reportedly building a stealth AI hardware startup (reported as Sedona.ai, 2025)
profile: Australian-born, London-raised founder of virtual-events platform Hopin, launched in 2019 and valued at $7.75B in 2021, which made him the UK's youngest billionaire at 27. After the post-pandemic slump Hopin sold its events business to RingCentral and he stepped down as CEO in 2023. He is reported to have raised ~$5M in 2025 for a stealth AI hardware venture.
interesting_fact: Hopin was fully remote from day one; at ~500 staff Boufarhat had never met most employees in person and lived as a digital nomad in rented homes with no permanent office.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Manchester mechanical engineering graduate, he did freelance coding jobs and wrote the first version of Hopin's software himself before hiring a team of six in 2019.
notes: Hurun listing was 2022-23; wealth likely far below $3B now given Hopin's sale (do not raise in outreach). New venture name (Sedona.ai) rests on thin reporting (https://streamlinefeed.co.ke/news/pandemic-darling-hopin-was-sold-for-scraps-now-founder-building-sedona-ai). Reported Swiss resident since 2022. No verified published contact found; LinkedIn/X are likely routes but were not verified.

name: Zhang Songqiao
current_role: Chairman, C C Land Holdings (HKEX: 1224); also chairman of Y.T. Realty and Yugang International
profile: Zhang Songqiao (Cheung Chung-kiu, b. 1964, Chongqing) moved to Hong Kong in 1980, began trading consumer goods into the mainland, then built Chongqing's first large housing estate, California Garden, via his Zhongyu (Chongqing Zhongyu) business. It was folded into Hong Kong-listed C C Land in 2006-07. C C Land bought London's 'Cheesegrater' (122 Leadenhall St) for GBP 1.15B in 2017.
interesting_fact: C C Land paid GBP 1.15 billion for London's Leadenhall Building ('the Cheesegrater') in 2017, one of the biggest single-building deals in the City.
deep_cut_fact: His first property project was converting farmland in northern Chongqing into California Garden (加州花园), the city's first large-scale housing estate; his company Yugang International listed in Hong Kong when he was 29.
notes: Low media profile; Chinese media call him the 'Li Ka-shing of Chongqing'. Hong Kong resident. 'Zhongyu' in source_of_wealth = 中渝 (Chongqing Zhongyu), not a gas company.

profile: Xiang Guangtong (项光通) appears on Hurun China/Global lists (2019-2026) with wealth attributed to Tsingshan Holding Group, the Wenzhou-founded stainless-steel and Indonesian nickel giant chaired by Xiang Guangda. No reliable public source confirms his title or relationship to Xiang Guangda.

name: Farhad Moshiri
current_role: Private investor based in Monaco; former majority owner of Everton FC (sold to Dan Friedkin, Dec 2024) and former chairman of USM Holdings
profile: Iran-born, UCL-educated chartered certified accountant who worked at Ernst & Young and Deloitte before partnering with Alisher Usmanov in the early 1990s, gaining stakes in Metalloinvest (which he chaired 2006-13), MegaFon and USM. He sold his Arsenal stake in 2016 to buy into Everton, rose to 94% ownership, cut ties with Usmanov in March 2022 and sold Everton in December 2024.
interesting_fact: He swapped clubs in 2016: sold his Arsenal stake to Usmanov to fund buying Everton, where he backed the new Bramley-Moore Dock stadium project before selling the club to Dan Friedkin.
deep_cut_fact: Before the oligarch world he was a career auditor: Ernst & Young (1979-85), Pannell Kerr Forster (1985-87) and Deloitte & Touche (1987-92), leaving as a senior manager in Deloitte's audit division; he later ran Europe Steel (2000-08).
notes: Very private, Monaco-based; rarely interviewed. No published personal or office contact found. Historic links to Usmanov (sanctioned 2022) - he severed ties March 2022. Avoid Everton-era fan criticism topics.

name: Varsha Engineer
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner (with husband Navin Engineer), Chemidex Pharma, Egham, Surrey
profile: Varsha Engineer and her husband Navin co-founded Chemidex in 1981 as a single pharmacy in Chertsey, Surrey. They grew it to 14 pharmacies, sold them to Celesio in 1999 (~GBP 12M), and turned Chemidex into a specialty pharma company acquiring and licensing prescription brands from 2000. The Sunday Times Rich List 2025 put the couple at GBP 3.45B.
interesting_fact: Chemidex started as one Chertsey pharmacy in 1981; after selling the chain in 1999 it bought its first drug brand in 2000 and became a billion-pound brand-licensing business.
deep_cut_fact: Navin (her co-founder husband) quit his first pharmacist job at Boots the same day an area manager asked him for a cup of tea while he was busy dispensing - the spark that led the couple to open their own pharmacy.
notes: Extremely private couple; no website (chemidex.co.uk down), no press office or social accounts found. Only public route is the company's registered office per Companies House (Chemidex Pharma Ltd, 01676110). Listed jointly with Navin Engineer; deep-cut fact is about Navin.

name: Wu Liangding
current_role: Co-founder/controlling family shareholder, Wanfeng Auto Holding Group and Rifa (日发) group, Xinchang, Zhejiang
profile: Wu Liangding (吴良定) ran the Xinchang textile-equipment factory that in 1992 became Zhongbao Industrial, forerunner of Wanfeng Auto. He led the Rifa textile-machinery business (now Rifa Precision Machinery) while wife Chen Ailian built Wanfeng into Asia's largest aluminium-wheel maker, later adding magnesium alloys and Diamond Aircraft. The family controls listed Wanfeng Aowei, Rifa Precision and Changchun Jingkai; son Wu Jinhua is a senior executive.
interesting_fact: Wanfeng, the family's wheel business, bought Austria's Diamond Aircraft in 2016-17 and is pursuing electric aircraft and eVTOL certification.
deep_cut_fact: Wanfeng's first aluminium motorcycle wheel was reverse-engineered from the wheel of an imported Yamaha motorcycle that Wu had given his wife Chen Ailian; her team spent 3 months measuring and copying it in 1993-94.
notes: Very low profile; wife Chen Ailian is the family's public face. 'Alive' inferred from continued Hurun 2026 listing - no recent personal news found. Avoid share-pledge/divestment topics.

name: Kabir Mulchandani
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, FIVE Holdings (Dubai), owner of FIVE Hotels & Resorts and Pacha Group
profile: Mumbai-born, Stanford- and Phillips Exeter-educated, Mulchandani worked in his family's consumer-electronics distribution business (Baron) before moving to Dubai in the early 2000s. He founded SKAI Holdings in 2011, rebranded it FIVE in 2017 and built a portfolio of 'party' luxury hotels in Dubai, Zurich, Ibiza and New York, buying Ibiza's Pacha Group for ~$330M in 2023. FIVE has weighed a London or New York IPO (2025).
interesting_fact: FIVE bought Pacha Group - the Ibiza nightclub and hotel brand with the cherries logo - for about $330 million in November 2023, folding the iconic club into his hotel empire.
deep_cut_fact: He studied industrial engineering at Stanford; in 2021 FIVE became the launch buyer of Airbus's first ACJ TwoTwenty business jet (with Comlux), which it later offered for charter.
